A directory tree is a "micro-tree" when its regular files add up to less than `micro_tree_max_bytes`, which is 2 MiB (`2 * 1024 * 1024`) (src/main.zig:38-42).

When it is one, zgrep takes a zero-thread fast path (src/main.zig:38-40):
- The tree is scanned on the calling thread, with no thread pool.
- The upward `.dataignore`/`.gitignore` walk is skipped.

`--force-swarm` opts out and restores the concurrent swarm (src/main.zig:41). 

The threshold is passed into the kamikaze search call alongside `opts.force_swarm` (src/main.zig:2452-2453). The context doesn't show the code that sums file sizes or makes the actual decision, so I can't say how the total is measured (e.g., whether it stops early) or the exact comparison logic.
